message.content:
Yes—you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta, but it’s handled through the city’s **Police Department** (not the city council itself). Here’s how you can do it: | Step | What to Do | Where/How | |------|------------|-----------| | **1. Identify the source** | Determine whether the noise is coming from a residential, commercial, or public‑space location. | N/A | | **2. Call 311** | Atlanta’s non-emergency hotline (311) will connect you to the appropriate department. | Phone: 404‑656‑3111 (or dial 311 on your cell phone) | | **3. Use the online portal** | You can submit a noise complaint online via the City of Atlanta’s official website. | Visit [Atlanta.gov](https://www.atlanta.gov) → “Services” → “Noise Complaint” (or search “noise complaint” on the site). | | **4. Provide details** | Be ready to give:
• Exact address or intersection
• Date & time of the noise
• Description of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs)
• Any evidence (photos, videos, audio recordings) | Online form or phone call | | **5. Follow up** | After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. If you don’t hear back within a few days, you can call 311 again or check the status online. | Phone or online portal | ### Quick Reference | Resource | Contact | |----------|---------| | **Atlanta Police Department – Noise Enforcement Unit** | Phone: 404‑656‑3111 (same as 311) | | **City of Atlanta 311** | Phone: 404‑656‑3111 | | **Online Complaint Form** | https://www.atlanta.gov/services/noise-complaint | ### A Few Tips * **Timing matters** – Noise ordinances typically have stricter limits during nighttime hours (often 10 p.m.–7 a.m.). * **Document everything** – Photos, videos, or audio recordings help the police assess the situation. * **Check the ordinance** – The City of Atlanta’s noise ordinance is available on the city’s website; it outlines permissible decibel levels and prohibited activities. If you’re unsure whether a particular noise violates the ordinance, you can ask the dispatcher when you call 311—they’ll let you know if it’s likely to be actionable. So, yes—just file a complaint through the city’s police department or 311, and they’ll take it from there.
